definition: A shareholder that builds a sizeable stake and presses management for change (board seats, cost cuts, a sale). Starboard's 2017-18 campaign at Mellanox preceded the company's auction.

China's State Administration for Market Regulation. Its anti-monopoly bureau reviews mergers between companies with sizeable China sales and can approve them with conditions, delay them or block them.
A merger condition that governs how the combined company behaves (for example no bundling, keep supplying rivals, stay interoperable) instead of forcing it to sell assets.
The time until cumulative profit or cash from an investment equals the price paid. A discounted payback first grows the price at a cost of capital, so it takes longer.
NVIDIA's (originally Mellanox's) family of network adapters for InfiniBand and Ethernet. Reference designs put one ConnectX NIC or SuperNIC beside every GPU, so it ships with GPU orders.
NVIDIA's (originally Mellanox's) DPU family: a ConnectX network adapter combined with Arm CPU cores that offloads networking, storage and security work from the host CPU.
